summary: Refined inline Steel viewer to neutral grey chrome with 640px maximum width, compact icon controls and agent configuration disclosure. Added native BB settings for Jev checkout path, credentials file path and text model, plus explicit Runner not integrated status; these are configuration preparation, not a functioning Jev adapter or credential validation. Built and reloaded plugin. Ran requested faster same-session Playwright/CDP demo: Example at 260ms, Wikipedia at 2126ms, GitHub at 5312ms with one-second pauses. No Jev execution or paid calls. Build succeeded; automated UI verification and formal tests remain pending. Code pushed as e92cb13f; target sync current. Awaiting user feedback, with full Jev runner implementation explicitly still outstanding.

state.request: Install and run https://github.com/steel-dev/steel-browser on the dyaus host for use from this BB environment, then create a new independently installable BB plugin in this repository that integrates Steel as the replacement browser infrastructure for the prior KERNEL.SH-based workflow. Keep the root orchestration-only conventions, align manifest/package/CLI/UI/docs/tests, avoid committing generated artifacts, and verify the Steel service plus the plugin's human UI and CLI surface.

lifecycle.riskRequest: Keep Steel hosted on the connected dyaus machine as the primary host; do not move or duplicate it to another machine. Extend the existing Steel browser plugin scope to evaluate and, where supported, integrate browser-use/jev-ultrafast as an optional browser-agent layer over the existing Steel CDP endpoint. Preserve the existing Steel service and plugin behavior, keep credentials out of repository state, and document any unsupported direct integration as an explicit limitation.

sizeDecision.reason: Keep Steel hosting and the optional jev-ultrafast adapter together because the adapter's only supported browser target is the existing Steel CDP session, and splitting them would make the integration contract unverifiable as separate slices.
